committed_turns.public_event: A newcomer has reached the card room.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: A coin rings off the table edge and wobbles across the floor toward the south door, and nobody at the card table moves to catch it. Four of them sit at a worn table near that door, pale as candle tallow, pointed teeth showing when they breathe, dressed in lace and velvet gone shiny at the elbows. Each has coins stacked in front of them; a silver ring sits among the stacks in the middle. The man dealing has stopped mid-hand, one card pinned between two fingers. Beyond them, the whole north wall is a carved mountain, tiny dwarves in tiny caverns, stone sunbeams fanning over a long tub sunk into the floor.
Narrator: When the dealer speaks it is slow and savoring, each word laid down like a card he means you to look at.
Dealer: Well, now. The door brought us company. Come in, come in, the passage is draftier than we are. That coin by your boot is the most interesting thing that has happened at this table in an hour, so tell me: are you the sort who picks it up, or the sort who waits to see whose it is?

committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "I pull up a chair, set five gold on the table, and say, "Deal me in. And five on the side says I win the first hand.""
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: For the first time since you walked in, he puts the card down. Chairs scrape as the other three pull in closer. Your five gold sits in the lamplight and everyone at the table looks at it once and then very carefully does not.
Dealer: Oh, I like you. You sit without being asked and you bet on yourself before you have seen a card. Five on the side, though? Five is what a person bets when they want to look brave. Make it ten, friend, and I'll believe you mean it. Otherwise we play for the ante and pretend you never said anything.

committed_turns.spoken:
Kit: Ten gold on a game nobody has explained to you. I love this for you.
Dealer: Who runs this room? I can save you the suspense and the ten gold: I do. Always have. But a bet is a bet, and I would hate to cheat you out of the pleasure of hearing it after you win. Ten on the side, then.
Narrator: Two cards slide face down across the wood and stop in front of you. The fourth player at the table glances at the dealer when he says always have, just for a moment, then back at their cards.

committed_turns.player_input: Before I look: what's the game called, and what beats what?
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Before I look: what's the game called, and what beats what?"
committed_turns.spoken:
Dealer: Called? Down here we just call it the game. Highest two cards take the pot, crowns over commons, and if we tie, the house breaks it. I keep it simple for guests; complicated rules make people suspicious, and suspicious people are terrible company.
Narrator: He reaches over and taps the backs of your two cards, one, two, with a single long finger, then sits back and folds his hands.
Dealer: There. Now you know everything I know. Look.

appraisal.cause: The visitor asks for the rules after staking ten gold, which is exactly the right question too late.

improv_read.connection: He wants control; rules he states himself are rules he can bend, so he answers simply and generously, which is what a man with the deck on his side can afford.
